response: The clustering still lacks a dedicated solar and stellar astrophysics cluster — papers on solar activity, sunspot tracking, stellar atmospheres, stellar magnetic fields, chromospheric physics, and stellar abundances are scattered across "Solar Wind Plasma Waves," "Simulation-Based Inference Methods," "Stellar evolution and feedback," and the catch-all "Diverse Astronomical Observations Survey" cluster, and they should all be consolidated into one solar/stellar cluster. The "Diverse Astronomical Observations Survey" remains a problematic catch-all: galactic/extragalactic papers within it (ISM, galaxy structure, star formation in galaxies, CGM) should join the "Galaxy Structure and Evolution" cluster, high-energy transient papers (FRBs, supernovae remnants) should join the high-energy cluster, and instrumentation/methods papers (satellite detection, polarimeter calibration) should form or join an instrumentation cluster. The "Simulation-Based Inference Methods Astrophysics" cluster is also incoherent, mixing cosmological inference, solar variability, and spectroscopic methods — these should be redistributed to their proper subject-area clusters rather than grouped by methodology alone.
